sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Matrona was a British and continental Celtic goddess. Her name means mother, and she was the mother of the obscure British god Maponus. The name Maponus seems to signify son of the mother. The name Matrona survives in the river Marne in France. That river formed the border between the settlements of Gaul and those of the Belgae. Celtic river divinities were usually goddesses. They embodied the life-giving force of the river's water and the fertility of the land of the watershed. Matrona may be the same goddess found in Wales as Modron.
objective: Document Matrona, the Celtic mother goddess whose name survives in the river Marne.
